item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-07
item.description: Two instruments landed in three weeks and neither is a licensing document. On 2026-10-24 MIIT's general office issued Notice No. 42 — published 2026-11-06 through CAICT's own account — requiring any phone, tablet or wearable with a preinstalled agent to carry an agent identity code under the GB/Z 185.2-2026 standard before it can obtain a network-access licence, and routing every OTA agent upgrade through MIIT-submitted plans, post-upgrade reports and expert evaluation before users may receive it. The standard is named as a reference (参考), the detection criterion it points to has not been published, and the document carries no effective date and no transition rules. Three weeks earlier, on 2026-10-20, Beijing Kaiyuan Industrial Software Research Institute completed civil registration as a science-and-technology non-enterprise unit under the city's civil affairs bureau, backed by a national ministry, the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology and Haidian District — operating a curation register that has collected 300-plus industrial-software open-source projects across CAE, CAD and EDA, an online platform still in internal test, and a 2,000-square-metre physical 'meta-space' with 96 desks and 30-plus applicant tenants. Read together with MIIT's own standards interpretation, which states that MCP and A2A exist internationally but have not formed unified consensus, the two artefacts describe an ecosystem whose open parts are organised as registers: one register of identities, one register of projects, both operated by identifiable institutions with market access attached at one end.
